findings.body: Every instance receives the timestamp captured when the module was imported rather than its creation time, so queued metadata is stale and cannot represent when each assignment was queued.
findings.failure_mode: Consumers inspecting or forwarding queued observe identical import-time timestamps for assignments created at different times.
findings.impact: Every instance receives the timestamp captured when the module was imported rather than its creation time, so queued metadata is stale and cannot represent when each assignment was queued.
findings.root_cause: The timezone.now() call is evaluated as a class-definition default instead of being deferred per dataclass instance.
findings.suggested_fix: Declare queued with dataclasses.field(default_factory=timezone.now) so timezone.now() runs for each instance.
findings.title: Use a default factory for the assignment timestamp
findings.trigger: Create multiple AssignmentSource instances through from_integration at different times without explicitly supplying queued.
findings.verifier_reason: Line 18 shows `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` as a class-level default in a frozen dataclass. This is evaluated once at module import time, not per-instance. The from_integration classmethod does not supply queued, so all instances share the same timestamp. This is a real mutable-default-like bug introduced by the patch.

pr.body:
## The problem:
When a Jira issue's `assignee` field is quickly modified multiple times in a row, we end up assigning and resyncing the assignees to Jira, which causes a loop. This is because _all_ inbound integration webhooks that modify an issue assignment generate an outbound update for all issue sync integrations as well.

## Solution:
This PR adds a new `AssignmentSource` dataclass, which acts as a context carrier when an external webhook triggers an issue assignment change. This is then checked on the outbound sync logic, preventing the change from being propagated to the same integration that initially triggered the change.
pr.title: fix(ecosystem): Breaks issue sync cycles

raw_findings.body: The assignment-specific context is advertised on sync_status_outbound, where it is not used, while the assignee-sync contract still exposes the context only through untyped **kwargs; callers and implementers can follow the wrong API and status synchronization gains misleading surface area.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Static API inspection and future implementations use an incorrect hook for assignment-source propagation, leaving the intended assignee contract implicit.

raw_findings.root_cause: The new assignment_source parameter was attached to the unrelated status synchronization method rather than the assignee synchronization method.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Remove assignment_source from sync_status_outbound and add it explicitly to sync_assignee_outbound, keeping the concrete implementations consistent with the task call.
raw_findings.title: Do not add the assignment context parameter to status synchronization

finding.verifier_reason: The claim that assignment_source on sync_status_outbound is misplaced is unsubstantiated. Repository context shows sync_status_outbound is called from sync_status_outbound task (L44) without passing assignment_source, and concrete implementations (jira, vsts) accept **kwargs. The parameter is unused but not harmful; the actual assignee sync uses sync_assignee_outbound which correctly receives assignment_source. This is at most a minor API design preference, not a defect.
